Positions in a bitmap

Source: R/index.R, R/wide.R
zuroar-index.Rd

A bitmap is a sorted vector without duplicates, so its values have positions, counting from 1. x[i] returns a bitmap of the values at positions i, as [ keeps the class of a Date: positive positions select, negative ones exclude, and a logical i is a mask over positions, recycled as R recycles one. Order and repetition in i do not matter, since the result is a set. Mixing signs, NA, and a position past the end are zuroar_error_index errors, because a bitmap holds no NA.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
x[i, ...]

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
x[[k, ...]]

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
head(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
tail(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
sort(x, decreasing = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
unique(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
rev(x)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
x[i, ...] <- value

# S3 method for class 'zuroar'
x[[i, ...]] <- value

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
x[i, ...]

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
x[[k, ...]]

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
head(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
tail(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
sort(x, decreasing = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
unique(x, incomparables = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
rev(x)

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
x[i, ...] <- value

# S3 method for class 'zuroar64'
x[[i, ...]] <- value

Arguments

x

A bitmap.

i

Positions: positive or negative whole numbers, or a logical mask. Missing, it selects every value.

...

Must be empty for [ and [[; ignored otherwise.

k

A single position.

n

For head() and tail(), how many values to keep, or, when negative, how many to drop from the other end.

decreasing

Must be FALSE.

incomparables

Ignored.

value

Not used: assignment is an error.

Value

[, head(), tail(), sort() and unique() a bitmap, [[ a single double.

Details

x[[k]] is the k-th smallest value as a double; roar_select() is its vectorised form. head() and tail() return bitmaps and follow R's rules for a negative n. sort() and unique() return x.

v %in% x and match(v, x) work, visiting every value of x; roar_contains() and roar_rank() answer the same questions without visiting the set.

Some vector operations have no meaning for a set and are zuroar_error_unsupported errors: x[i] <- v and x[[k]] <- v (use roar_add() and roar_remove()), rev(x) and sort(x, decreasing = TRUE) (use rev(as.double(x))).

Examples

x <- roar(c(1, 7, 9, 100000))
x[2:3]
#> <zuroar> 2 values in [7, 9]: 7 9
x[-1]
#> <zuroar> 3 values in [7, 100000]: 7 9 100000
x[c(TRUE, FALSE)]
#> <zuroar> 2 values in [1, 9]: 1 9
x[[2]]
#> [1] 7
head(x, 2)
#> <zuroar> 2 values in [1, 7]: 1 7
tail(x, -1)
#> <zuroar> 3 values in [7, 100000]: 7 9 100000
roar_contains(x, 9)
#> [1] TRUE
